plain: A person taken prisoner, as in war.

webster.text: A prisoner taken by force or stratagem in war, by an enemy; followed by to; as a captive to the victor.

more.text: One who is charmed or subdued by beauty or excellence; one whose affections are seized, or who is held by strong ties of love.
To take prisoner; to bring into subjection.

example.quote: " Some were taken captive, children taken out of their schools, and carried away.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 2, Massachusetts Convention, Hon. Mr. SMITH, January 25, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
